content: python-oracledb type-binding pitfalls beyond setinputsizes: dates must be bound as Python datetime.date/datetime objects (not strings) or explicit cursor.var(oracledb.DB_TYPE_DATE) -- passing strings relies on implicit NLS conversion that breaks across locale/date-format settings. Decimal/NUMBER columns bound from Python float lose precision for currency-like values; bind Decimal via cursor.var(oracledb.DB_TYPE_NUMBER, arraysize=...) or convert explicitly to avoid float rounding errors on financial data. Mixed None/typed values across executemany batches for the same column position can flip inferred bind type between batches and raise DPY-3013.
